reel.caption:
Bought something on 'no-cost' EMI this festive sale: do you still pay extra?

On a no-cost EMI the bank still charges interest; the seller gives an upfront discount equal to that interest.
The 18% GST on the interest is not covered by that discount, so it lands on your card bill.
Illustrative: ₹1 lakh over 12 months at 15% a year → interest ≈ ₹7,672 → GST ≈ ₹1,381 extra, plus any processing fee (also with GST).
Ask to see the interest and GST split before you choose EMI.

Did your last EMI purchase show a GST line on the bill?

Sources: a credit-comparison site's no-cost EMI explainer, a personal-finance magazine's credit-card EMI guide and a brokerage's learning newsletter; ₹ figures are our own EMI-formula arithmetic.
